topic: Snowball Earth: the planet that froze solid, and the new idea about how it escaped

through_line.name: the ice sheet
through_line.progression: thin caps at the poles, creeping sea ice, the equator sealed, a thick white shell, volcano vents punching through it, cracking and slushy, meltwater pouring off it, a thin frozen sheet returning, thinning again over ponds, gone
through_line.resolution: In the payoff there is no ice anywhere: Nia stands in a hot tropical plaza holding a pale cap-carbonate pebble, the only trace the ice left behind.

blocks.vo_line: The whole planet froze. Seven hundred seventeen million years ago, ice crept from both poles until it sealed the oceans at the equator.
blocks.through_line_state: white caps spreading from both poles and meeting at the equator
shots: WIDE, static: Earth hangs in dark space, blue oceans and brown continents, small white caps at both poles.
CU, slow push-in: the northern ice cap creeps south across the blue ocean in a smooth white tide.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: the southern cap races north, the two white edges closing on the equator.
ECU, macro: the last thin strip of blue water at the equator pinches shut with a soft crackle.
WIDE, gentle drift: the whole planet now white, turning slowly, a pale ice sheet glinting in faint sunlight.

blocks.vo_line: Picture a white world. Sea ice to every horizon, a weak sun, and average temperatures that may have fallen near minus fifty Celsius.
blocks.through_line_state: flat white sea ice stretching to every horizon
shots: WIDE, static: a flat frozen ocean under a pale sky, Nia in her lavender coat standing tiny in the middle.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia turns in a slow circle, white ice in every direction behind her.
CU, slow push-in: her breath puffs into frosty clouds as she rubs her mittens together.
ECU, macro: frost feathers grow across the ice surface beside her boot.
WIDE, gentle drift: a small pale sun sits low over the endless ice while wind drags a thin veil of snow.

blocks.vo_line: Geologists call it Snowball Earth. The name came from Caltech scientist Joe Kirschvink in nineteen ninety two, but the clues surfaced decades earlier.
blocks.through_line_state: a white-painted globe on the lab desk, ice drawn over every ocean
shots: WIDE, static: the science lab, Theo at his desk beside a globe painted completely white.
CU, slow push-in: Theo spins the white globe and grins at it.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: Theo pulls an old dusty folder from a shelf and blows dust off it.
ECU, macro: the folder falls open onto hand-drawn sketches of striped rock layers.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Theo holds a sketch up beside the white globe, comparing them, nodding.

blocks.vo_line: Rocks dumped by glaciers turned up in places that once sat near the equator, where ice should never reach sea level.
blocks.through_line_state: a glacier tongue grinding down a valley to the sea
shots: WIDE, static: a broad valley with a thick glacier sliding down toward a grey coastline.
CU, low angle: the glacier's front edge pushes a jumble of boulders and gravel ahead of it.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: Nia walks along a ridge of mixed rubble left behind by the ice.
ECU, macro: a scratched, polished pebble rolls loose from the rubble pile.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia picks up the pebble and turns it in her mitten as the glacier creaks behind her.

blocks.vo_line: How do we know where they sat? Tiny magnetic grains in the rock froze in alignment with Earth's field, recording their ancient latitude.
blocks.through_line_state: a white band of ice painted around the globe's equator
shots: MEDIUM, static: Theo sets a rock sample on the desk beside the globe.
ECU, macro: inside the rock, tiny dark grains all point the same way like little compass needles.
CU, slow push-in: Theo leans in with a magnifying glass, one eye huge through the lens.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: Theo slides a marker along the globe and stops right on the equator.
CU, gentle drift: the white ice band on the globe glints where his marker rests.

blocks.vo_line: Then there are dropstones: boulders that fell straight down into fine seafloor mud, the way rocks drop from melting icebergs today.
blocks.through_line_state: an iceberg of the sheet drifting offshore, dropping stones
shots: WIDE, static: a grey shoreline, an iceberg drifting slowly in the calm water offshore.
MEDIUM, low angle: the iceberg's underside melts, and a boulder slips free of the ice.
CU, slow push-in: the boulder sinks through dim green water trailing a stream of bubbles.
ECU, macro: it lands in soft layered mud on the seafloor, puffing up a small cloud.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: the mud settles around the half-buried boulder, layers bent beneath it.

blocks.vo_line: How does a planet freeze? Through a feedback loop where fresh snow reflects most sunlight back to space, while dark ocean absorbs it.
blocks.through_line_state: bright white polar sheets beside dark open ocean
shots: MEDIUM, static: sunbeams drawn as soft yellow arrows stream toward Earth from the side.
CU, slow push-in: arrows hitting the white polar ice bounce straight back out into space.
ECU, macro: arrows hitting the dark blue ocean sink in and glow warm orange.
WIDE, lateral drift: the whole planet with bounced arrows over the ice and glowing ocean below.
CU, gentle drift: the white sheet edge creeps a little further over the dark water.

blocks.vo_line: Every new patch of ice cools the planet further. Models suggest once sea ice passes roughly thirty degrees latitude, the freeze runs away.
blocks.through_line_state: sea ice racing across open water toward the tropics
shots: MEDIUM, static: Nia stands at the edge of the ice where it meets dark open water.
ECU, macro: crystals spread across the water surface, linking into a thin white skin.
CU, low angle: Nia steps back as the ice edge slides past her boots.
WIDE, lateral drift: the white edge sweeps across the open sea like a closing curtain.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia looks back at the horizon, now white all the way around.

blocks.vo_line: But something had to start it. Just before the freeze, enormous lava floods buried part of northern Canada under fresh dark basalt.
blocks.through_line_state: no ice yet, only a faint frost line on distant hills
shots: WIDE, static: a vast plain of dark basalt, glowing orange cracks, a frosty ridge far on the horizon.
CU, slow push-in: a slow river of lava oozes over older black rock.
MEDIUM, low angle: layer upon layer of lava flows stack into a giant dark staircase.
ECU, macro: a crust forms on the lava surface and cracks into hexagon shapes.
WIDE, gentle drift: the dark plain cools and steams under a grey sky, the frosty ridge glinting beyond.

blocks.vo_line: Rain slowly dissolves fresh basalt, and that chemistry pulls carbon dioxide out of the air. Less greenhouse gas meant a colder planet.
blocks.through_line_state: frost beginning to creep down onto the dark basalt
shots: MEDIUM, static: grey rain falls steadily on the dark basalt plain.
ECU, macro: raindrops fizz on the rock surface, tiny bubbles rising.
CU, low angle: small grey puffs drift down out of the sky and vanish into the wet rock.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: the rain turns to snowflakes over the dark plain.
CU, gentle drift: a thin white frost spreads across the black rock and settles.

blocks.vo_line: The ice met at the equator and closed. Seen from space, Earth became a frosted marble, white from one pole to the other.
blocks.through_line_state: a complete white shell around the planet
shots: MEDIUM, static: the white Earth turns slowly, no blue showing anywhere.
ECU, macro: the frosted surface sparkles like sugar crystals in the sunlight.
CU, slow push-in: the line where the two ice sheets met forms a faint seam at the equator.
WIDE, lateral drift: the frosted marble drifts past a small bright sun.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: the white planet settles, turning silently in the dark.

blocks.vo_line: Out on the ocean, the ice may have grown hundreds of meters thick, and the whole sheet crept slowly toward the equator.
blocks.through_line_state: a thick white shell over the sea, slowly flowing
shots: CU, static: Nia kneels and taps the ice with a small pick, which barely scratches it.
WIDE, low angle: a cutaway shows the ice as a towering white slab above dark water far below.
ECU, macro: a crack in the cutaway reveals layer upon layer of compressed blue ice.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: the whole ice surface slides very slowly past Nia, who stands still.
CU, gentle drift: Nia watches a ridge of ice inch by, eyebrows raised.

blocks.vo_line: And it lasted: the first great freeze, the Sturtian, held on for roughly fifty six million years. A second freeze followed soon after.
blocks.through_line_state: the white globe gets a second coat of white paint
shots: CU, static: Theo flips an hourglass on his desk, sand pouring through.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: Theo leans back, waiting, as the hourglass empties.
ECU, macro: the last grains drop and Theo flips it again immediately.
WIDE, lateral drift: the reverse side of the lab, a wall of hourglasses all draining at once.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Theo brushes a second coat of white paint over the globe, sighing.

blocks.vo_line: That raises a puzzle, because an ice planet reflects so much sunlight it should stay frozen forever. So how did Earth ever escape?
blocks.through_line_state: the white shell bouncing nearly all sunlight away
shots: CU, static: soft yellow sunbeam arrows hit the white planet and all bounce away.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: the white Earth sits locked and still, a few arrows glancing off.
ECU, macro: one arrow skims the ice and ricochets off into space.
WIDE, lateral drift: the white planet small against a huge black sky, the sun far off.
CU, gentle drift: a single faint puff of grey smoke rises from one spot on the ice.

blocks.vo_line: Volcanoes. They kept erupting through the ice, breathing out carbon dioxide, and with no rain or open rock, nothing could absorb it.
blocks.through_line_state: a volcano vent punching up through the white shell
shots: WIDE, static: a dark volcano cone pokes up through the flat ice field, steam rising.
CU, low angle: the volcano erupts with a soft boom, ash and grey gas billowing upward.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: grey gas clouds spread out over the white ice and hang there.
ECU, macro: ash flakes land on the ice and sit on the surface, unmelted.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia watches from a safe distance, wrapping her scarf tighter.

blocks.vo_line: Over millions of years the gas piled up, perhaps to hundreds of times today's level, until the greenhouse finally beat the ice.
blocks.through_line_state: the ice around the vent darkening and starting to sag
shots: MEDIUM, static: a thick grey haze now fills the sky above the volcano.
ECU, macro: a sunbeam enters the haze and gets trapped, bouncing around inside it, glowing.
CU, slow push-in: the ice beside the volcano turns grey and starts to sag.
WIDE, lateral drift: the hazy sky stretches over the whole ice field, warm and orange.
CU, gentle drift: a first drip of water slides off an icicle on the volcano's flank.

blocks.vo_line: Once melting started, dark exposed ground soaked up heat and sped it along. The thaw may have taken only a few thousand years.
blocks.through_line_state: the glacier cracking and pouring meltwater
shots: CU, static: dark rock pokes out of the shrinking glacier, glowing warm in the sun.
MEDIUM, low angle: meltwater gushes off the glacier front in a roaring waterfall.
ECU, macro: a crack zips across the glacier surface and widens.
WIDE, lateral drift: the valley turns from white to brown as the ice retreats uphill.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia jumps over a new stream, laughing, as the water rushes past.

blocks.vo_line: Then the planet swung to the opposite extreme. A scorching greenhouse, fierce storms, and acid rain that ate into freshly uncovered rock.
blocks.through_line_state: last chunks of the ice sheet melting in hot surf
shots: MEDIUM, static: Nia, now without her coat, fans herself on the hot shore.
CU, low angle: towering storm clouds roll in over the sea, flashing with lightning.
ECU, macro: rain hits a boulder and fizzes, the surface pitting.
WIDE, lateral drift: heavy rain sweeps along the coast as the last ice chunks melt in the surf.
CU, gentle drift: Nia holds a leaf over her head as an umbrella, squinting at the sky.

blocks.vo_line: That chemistry poured into the oceans and settled as limestone. Today it sits as a pale layer on top of the glacial debris.
blocks.through_line_state: a jumbled dark band of ice-dropped rubble in the cliff
shots: WIDE, static: a modern desert cliff with dark jumbled rock below and a pale cream layer on top.
CU, slow push-in: the boundary line between the dark rubble and the pale layer.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia, in a sun hat, climbs up the slope toward the pale layer.
ECU, macro: fine wavy ripples in the pale stone, like frozen waves.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia places her palm flat on the pale layer and looks up at it.

blocks.vo_line: Geologists call these cap carbonates, and they turn up worldwide, from Namibia to Australia. Ice below, warm-water rock sitting directly above.
blocks.through_line_state: the ice record reduced to a band in the rock
shots: CU, static: Nia taps the boundary with a small rock hammer, a chip falling away.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: Nia holds the chip next to a dark pebble from the rubble below.
ECU, macro: the pale chip and the dark pebble side by side in her palm.
WIDE, slow push-in: the same two-tone cliff repeated along a distant coastline, pale stripe over dark.
CU, gentle drift: Nia slips the pale chip into her pocket and smiles.

blocks.vo_line: But a two thousand twenty six study suggests the Sturtian was not one long freeze. Earth may have frozen and thawed repeatedly.
blocks.through_line_state: the globe flickering between white and blue
shots: MEDIUM, static: Theo reads a fresh printout, then freezes mid-sip of his tea.
ECU, macro: the printout shows a wavy line rising and falling again and again.
CU, slow push-in: Theo's eyebrows shoot up and he sets the tea down.
WIDE, lateral drift: Theo spins the globe, and it flickers from white to blue to white again.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Theo stops the globe and stares at it, tapping his chin.

blocks.vo_line: Harvard researchers modeled the carbon cycle and found the lava fields kept resetting the trap, pulling carbon down every time the ice retreated.
blocks.through_line_state: a model ice sheet on the desk melting and refreezing
shots: CU, static: Theo types on a laptop, a looping diagram on its screen.
MEDIUM, low angle: Theo builds a tabletop model, a little dark lava field beside a tray of ice.
ECU, macro: the ice tray melts to water, then frost creeps back across it.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: Theo moves the tray back and forth from a lamp to the shade.
CU, gentle drift: Theo nods slowly, watching the ice reform again.

blocks.vo_line: Each thaw exposed fresh basalt to the rain, which drew carbon dioxide back down, and the planet slid into another snowball phase.
blocks.through_line_state: melting ice uncovering basalt, then frost returning
shots: MEDIUM, static: the ice sheet melts back from the dark basalt plain, uncovering it.
ECU, macro: rain falls on the bared rock, fizzing in tiny bubbles.
CU, low angle: grey puffs drift down from the sky into the wet rock.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: snow begins falling again, dusting the basalt white.
CU, gentle drift: the white sheet slides back over the plain and settles.

blocks.vo_line: Frozen, then sweltering, then locked in white again. That rhythm could explain how one ice age lasted tens of millions of years.
blocks.through_line_state: the planet pulsing between white shell and blue ocean
shots: CU, static: Earth turns white, then blue, then white again, like a slow heartbeat.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: a ticking clock face hovers beside the pulsing planet.
ECU, macro: the clock hands spin faster and faster.
WIDE, lateral drift: the pulsing Earth drifts across the dark sky, white and blue in turn.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: the planet settles on white for a moment, glowing softly.

blocks.vo_line: It may also explain how life hung on. Microbes and simple algae already existed, and somehow they survived the whole ordeal.
blocks.through_line_state: a thin ice sheet with a small pond of meltwater on top
shots: WIDE, static: a small turquoise pond sits in a hollow on the white ice, sunlight sparkling on it.
CU, slow push-in: tiny green and amber smudges float in the clear water.
ECU, macro: round microbes with little faces wiggle and bump into each other.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia kneels at the edge with a jar and scoops up some water.
CU, gentle drift: Nia holds the jar to the light, the microbes swirling inside.

blocks.vo_line: The warm breaks may have kept oxygen from collapsing. Life could also shelter in meltwater ponds, thin tropical ice, and volcanic hot springs.
blocks.through_line_state: the ice sheet thinning, light glowing through it
shots: CU, static: the microbes in the jar give off a few tiny bubbles.
ECU, macro: one bubble rises and pops at the water surface with a sparkle.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: Nia lifts a thin pane of ice, and green light glows through it.
WIDE, low angle: far off, steam rises from a hot spring between ice ridges.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia smiles at the jar and tucks it inside her coat.

blocks.vo_line: Not everyone agrees. Some researchers argue a strip of open water survived near the equator, a slushball rather than a snowball.
blocks.through_line_state: the sheet split by a narrow strip of slushy open water
shots: MEDIUM, static: Nia walks along the ice and stops at a narrow channel of dark slushy water.
ECU, macro: slushy ice crystals bob and swirl on the water surface.
CU, low angle: Nia tilts her head, thinking, one hand on her hip.
WIDE, lateral drift: the open strip stretches into the distance like a dark ribbon through white.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia shrugs at the camera, palms up, half smiling.

blocks.vo_line: The last freeze ended around six hundred thirty five million years ago. Soon after, by geological standards, the first large complex organisms appeared.
blocks.through_line_state: only a few small floes left drifting far offshore
shots: CU, static: in clear shallow water, soft frond-shaped creatures sway on the seafloor.
MEDIUM, slow push-in: a flat quilted disc-shaped creature rests on a green microbial mat.
ECU, macro: the frond's edges ripple gently in the current.
WIDE, lateral drift: the shallow sea floor dotted with frond creatures, a few small ice floes far offshore.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: Nia wades in barefoot and peers down at them, delighted.

blocks.vo_line: Some scientists suspect the freeze, and the nutrients its melting glaciers released, helped set the stage for animals. That link is debated.
blocks.through_line_state: the ice remembered only as the dark band beneath the pale stripe
shots: MEDIUM, static: Nia sits at the foot of the two-tone cliff with a notebook on her knee.
ECU, macro: her pencil draws a small arrow from a snowflake to a little fish.
CU, low angle: Nia looks up at the pale stripe, then back at her drawing.
MEDIUM, lateral drift: she adds a question mark next to the arrow and taps it with her pencil.
CU, gentle drift: Nia closes the notebook and smiles at the cliff.

blocks.vo_line: Every animal alive today, including you, descends from life that made it through the frozen planet. The ice left, but its survivors stayed.
blocks.through_line_state: no ice anywhere, only a pale cap-carbonate pebble in Nia's hand
shots: WIDE, static: a sunny tropical plaza, palm trees, people and birds and a dog out in the heat.
MEDIUM, low angle: Nia, in summer clothes, sits on a fountain edge in the sun.
CU, slow push-in: she opens her hand to show the small pale stone chip from the cliff.
ECU, macro: the pebble's fine wavy layers catch the bright sunlight.
MEDIUM, gentle drift: a bird lands beside Nia, and she laughs as the plaza bustles around them.
